name: Cucumber slices

card.summary: Classic spa cold compress for puffy eyes; any effect is from cold, and it is untested.
card.note: No research on cucumber for the eyes specifically.

quick.overview:
Cucumber slices over the eyes are a traditional remedy for puffy, tired-looking eyes.

No studies have tested them; any short-term effect is usually attributed to the cold.
quick.mechanism: Chilled, watery slices act as a mild cold compress that may briefly narrow vessels.
quick.risks: No specific harms documented; hygiene and eye contact with produce are general considerations.

lead: Cucumber slices on the eyes are a long-standing home beauty practice for puffy, tired-looking eyes. Chilled slices are laid over closed eyelids for a short rest, and people use them to make the under-eye area look calmer and less swollen, usually before an event or after a poor night's sleep.

The practice is generally explained by cold and moisture. Cucumber is about 95% water, and a chilled slice works as a gentle cool compress.[1] Wikipedia describes cold compresses as a short-term remedy for puffy eyes, because cold constricts blood vessels and reduces fluid flow into tissue.[2][3] The same article lists the common causes of morning puffiness, including fluid shifting while lying down, sleep loss, salt intake, allergies and ageing, and suggests head elevation during sleep as a preventive measure.[3] The cucumber pages and the puffy-eye page cited here do not themselves make claims about cucumber, and no study has tested cucumber slices specifically.

chain: Chilled slice rests on the closed eyelid
Cold narrows surface blood vessels and eases fluid
Eyes look less puffy for a short time
angle.text: A cold, moist slice over each closed eye gives a brief cooling effect that people use to reduce the look of puffiness before going out. The effect described is temporary and comes from the cold, as with any cool compress.

paras: Slices are chilled in a refrigerator, and placed over closed eyes while the person lies down. Raw cucumber is mostly water with small amounts of carbohydrate and protein, and vitamin K as its notable micronutrient.[1] The image of a person reclining with cucumber slices on their eyes is a familiar spa and skincare picture.

sections.h: How it is thought to work
paras: Most explanations credit the cold and moisture rather than cucumber itself, in the same way as a cold spoon, tea bag or gel mask. Cold is described as constricting blood vessels and reducing fluid leakage into tissue, and is presented as a short-term fix for puffiness.[3] Reviews of cold compression in injury settings report mixed results, so findings from other body areas are not a direct guide to the eyelids.[2]

Puffiness that comes from fluid shifting overnight, salt, crying or tiredness tends to be the type that people say they treat this way.[3] Persistent or one-sided swelling has medical causes such as allergy, infection or thyroid conditions, which the puffy-eye article lists separately.[3]

Cucumber is a common food and the practice involves unbroken skin on closed lids. As with anything placed near the eyes, people who are allergic to cucumber or who have eye irritation may have reactions; the sources consulted do not document specific harms from the practice.
No studies found on cucumber slices for puffy or dark eyes.

lore.intro: Cucumber slices are a staple of home eye-care lore and are often mentioned alongside tea bags, cold spoons and chilled gel masks.

claims.claim: Cucumber slices reduce eye puffiness and dark circles
claims.believers: Proponents describe a cooling, soothing effect that leaves the area looking less swollen.
claims.experts: Reference pages on cucumber and on puffy eyes make no cucumber claim; cold compresses in general are described as a short-term aid for swelling.[1][3]
